sahil: Heads-up — dashboards showing a persistent ~200 unaccounted tokens/min spike coming from long-lived websocket sessions after fallback routing. Looks like we lose route attribution on idle heartbeats. anyone seen this?
marie: yep saw similar in eu-region yesterday. can you share an example event?
sahil: here's an anonymized snippet from the edge logs we pulled: ```json
{"ts":"2026-02-15T18:02:11Z","session_id":"s-abc123","event":"heartbeat","route_id":null,"tokens":0,"client_header":null}
```
marie: ah — route_id null on heartbeat. downstream metering treats that as unattributed and it becomes an orphan token when subsequent requests are batched.
jon: quick q: do we want to fix at the edge (populate route on heartbeat) or at the ingest side (join heartbeat to last-seen-route)? edge fix is cleaner but requires router change + rollout. ingest-side is more resilient but more complex and changes billing join logic.
lina: prefer edge if rollout cost is small. we already have sticky-session mapping on the proxy, it can attach `X-Route-Origin` on heartbeat. avoids backfilling later.
ted: the risky part is rolling router change across Dedicated + Private. clientlib upgrades are impossible for some customers. edge change is in our infra plane so fine, but need canary plan.
sahil: proposed edge header: `X-Route-Origin: sticky-session` and `X-Route-Id: <id>` on heartbeat. sample curl for testing: ```bash
curl -X POST https://edge.internal/events 
 -H "Authorization: Bearer $INTERNAL_TOKEN" 
 -H "X-Route-Origin: sticky-session" 
 -H "X-Route-Id: r-78f" 
 -d '{"session_id":"s-123","type":"heartbeat","tokens":0}'
```
marie: if we add headers, metering-ingest should prefer header over body join. but need schema bump for `route_origin` in the event proto.
jon: that means three things: 1) router adds headers on heartbeat, 2) ingest accepts header and sets route_id if missing, 3) console shows heartbeat attribution metrics.
lina: console changes: new card in tenant billing preview "heartbeat attribution" with two lines: heartbeat count and reattributed token delta. also a toggle in preview to include/exclude heartbeats from sample counts.
ted: rollout plan suggestion: canary 1% across hosted for 6h, monitor orphan_token_rate, then 10% for 12h, then 50% then 100%. for Dedicated/Private, opt-in toggle in release notes and a migration playbook.
sahil: also thinking about backfill: for last 48h we can re-run dedupe + join using session_id to reassign orphan tokens where route appears later in session. low priority but helpful for invoice stability.
marie: agree reassign script, but we must mark those as adjustments in invoice preview (not billing ledger) — keep audit trail.
jon: one open debate: do we treat heartbeat as special event type `heartbeat` or generic `session_ping` with `route_origin` metadata? special type simplifies console UX.
lina: UX wins with `heartbeat` — easier filter for alerts.
ted: telemetry: add metric `metering.heartbeat_attribution_success` and `metering.orphan_token_rate`. alert if orphan_token_rate > 0.5% for >10m during canary.
ops-bot: deploy-bot scheduled deploy to edge-router-canary at 2026-03-01T22:00Z for PR #4821 :rocket: 
sahil: thanks — i'll own the ingest change and the backfill script. @lina can you own console card?
lina: on it, will draft wire and link mockups in product-docs. :+1:
marie: i'll add proto change and coord with infra for header certs.
jon: I'll run the canary watch and add dashboards for the new metrics.
ted: leaving notes for Dedicated/Private: add opt-in flag `enable_heartbeat_route_injection` in operator docs.
sahil: OK team — next step: small PR to edge to attach headers on heartbeat (test only). i'll open ingest PR and backfill plan doc. thanks! :thumbsup:
